heard: A cosmic abyss two billion light years wide is stealing light's energy. Spanning nearly two billion light years across, the Aridness Supervoid holds the record as space's most massive emptiness. Inside this titanic cosmic hole, vast amounts of galaxies, gas, and invisible dark matter are missing. When ancient light from 380,000 years after the Big Bang enters the void, dark energy accelerates space's expansion. The stretched gravitational landscape drains energy from passing photons, cooling them as they exit. This creates a region roughly 70 microkelvin colder than the universe's average background temperature, wrapped in a warm ring. Yet standard cosmological calculations reveal this void expansion can only explain a fraction of the deep chill. No known physical process should drain energy from the Big Bang's relic radiation so aggressively.
